evidence.claim: Prayut told parliament that the opposition debate contained incorrect information and said the opposition had distorted facts to create public confusion; the story frames this as his direct reply to the censure motion.
evidence.title: Prayut counters censure attack as lacking in correct information
evidence.excerpt: Prayut told parliament that the opposition debate contained incorrect information and said the opposition had distorted facts to create public confusion; the story frames this as his direct reply to the censure motion.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Thai reporting with direct attributed remarks from Prayut in Parliament.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the target year and during the censure debate.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Prayut's public statements.
contrary_evidence: This is a self-defense claim, not external verification that his critics were wrong.

evidence.claim: The government spokesman said Prayut was confident he had done nothing wrong and would answer every issue raised by the opposition, while accusing opponents of distorting information.
evidence.title: Prayut will answer opposition questions during censure showdown: govt spokesman
evidence.excerpt: The government spokesman said Prayut was confident he had done nothing wrong and would answer every issue raised by the opposition, while accusing opponents of distorting information.
evidence.source_locator: article body and quoted spokesman remarks
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Attributed contemporaneous reporting on the prime minister's public posture before the censure debate.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to Prayut through his spokesman and public stance.
contrary_evidence: The report records his denial, not a finding that no wrongdoing occurred.

evidence.claim: Thailand's Constitutional Court ruled that Prayut had not exceeded the eight-year limit, allowing him to return from suspension and continue in office.
evidence.title: Thai court rules prime minister can stay in office
evidence.excerpt: Thailand's Constitutional Court ruled that Prayut had not exceeded the eight-year limit, allowing him to return from suspension and continue in office.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire story reproducing the court ruling with clear legal consequence.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is a legal outcome about Prayut's tenure, not a proof of personal honesty; it matters here because it bears on his stated commitment to formal limits.
contrary_evidence: The court ruling does not resolve whether his tenure strategy was ethically candid or opportunistic.

evidence.claim: A party source said Prayut was being courted to join the newly established Ruam Thai Sang Chart Party after the APEC summit, and that some MPs were expected to follow him there.
evidence.title: Prayut will join new party: source
evidence.excerpt: A party source said Prayut was being courted to join the newly established Ruam Thai Sang Chart Party after the APEC summit, and that some MPs were expected to follow him there.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous reporting on party-switch plans, though based on a source rather than a direct public announcement.
evidence.ruler_attribution: About Prayut's own political choice and surrounding support network.
contrary_evidence: This is still source-based reporting before his final public confirmation.

evidence.claim: The report says Prayut's political future remained under wraps amid reports that he might join Ruam Thai Sang Chart, with insiders describing continuing coalition maneuvering over his post-election role.
evidence.title: Prayut's future still under wraps after report of crucial meeting
evidence.excerpt: The report says Prayut's political future remained under wraps amid reports that he might join Ruam Thai Sang Chart, with insiders describing continuing coalition maneuvering over his post-election role.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous but source-heavy reporting on an unresolved political move.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Relevant to Prayut's own political positioning, but the report is not itself a direct statement from him.
contrary_evidence: It is better treated as transitional context than as a concrete act.

evidence.claim: Prayut confirmed he would register with Ruam Thai Sang Chart and run for head of government under that party's banner, after previously remaining non-committal about his political future.
evidence.title: At last, Prayut will run for PM under Ruam Thai Sang Chart banners
evidence.excerpt: Prayut confirmed he would register with Ruam Thai Sang Chart and run for head of government under that party's banner, after previously remaining non-committal about his political future.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct reporting on a late-2022 public confirmation, though from a smaller local outlet.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Prayut's own political choice.
contrary_evidence: The source is secondary and smaller than Reuters, so it is best used as supportive context rather than a standalone anchor.

evidence.claim: At an anti-corruption event, Prayut said Thailand was mired in corruption, pledged to fight graft, and said he was paying close attention to punishing wrongdoers and ensuring transparent operations.
evidence.title: Prayut promises to free Thailand of corruption, introduce transparency
evidence.excerpt: At an anti-corruption event, Prayut said Thailand was mired in corruption, pledged to fight graft, and said he was paying close attention to punishing wrongdoers and ensuring transparent operations.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct reporting of a public anti-corruption speech with clear quotes.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Prayut's own public claims, though they are self-reports rather than independent findings.
contrary_evidence: The speech is a promise and self-description, not evidence that corruption was actually reduced.

evidence.claim: The study says Prayut and Prawit appointed their favourites to senior army and police posts, and that 2022 reshuffles were heavily influenced by political and personal ties and factional bargaining.
evidence.title: 2022/95 'Dissecting Thailand's 2022 Military and Police Reshuffles: Palace Proactivity?'
evidence.excerpt: The study says Prayut and Prawit appointed their favourites to senior army and police posts, and that 2022 reshuffles were heavily influenced by political and personal ties and factional bargaining.
evidence.source_locator: executive summary and reshuffle analysis sections
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Analytical scholarly source with concrete tables and a detailed 2022 appointment map.
evidence.period_fit: Directly focused on 2022 appointments and reshuffles.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strongly attributable to Prayut and his close governing network because the paper explicitly names them as appointment influencers.
contrary_evidence: The paper also stresses that palace influence was substantial, so not every appointment can be attributed solely to Prayut.

unresolved_gaps: No direct 2022 ruler-attributed existential-risk choice, escalation, or crisis-management episode is shown.
Command-and-control, custody, and safety-governance evidence tied specifically to Prayut remains thin.
PM-level attribution for 2022 international-security choices is still thin; most evidence is ministry or delegation posture.
The Myanmar and Ukraine material does not yet show concrete peace or accountability outcomes attributable to Prayut.
Direct chain-of-command evidence for the APEC crackdown and the deep-south emergency regime remains limited.
The torture/disappearance law is an important reform, but year-end enforcement evidence is still weak.
Direct evidence on the sponsors and mechanism of the election-system change is still thin.
4B.4 and 4B.7 remain under-evidenced relative to the stronger protest, media, and term-limit material.
Budget intent and macro recovery are better evidenced than actual implementation and take-up.
Evidence on appointments, anti-capture, and mistake-correction is still weak.
Direct service-delivery, take-up, and quality evidence is thin outside budget allocations and national surveys.
Ruler-specific causal attribution for rural, child, and mental-health outcomes remains weak.
No independent 2022 finding of personal lying, self-dealing, or concealed conflict of interest is shown.
The package relies too much on allegations, self-defense, and broader regime context.
The program basis is only partly explicit; some objectives are inferred from budgets and coalition moves rather than a single frozen program statement.
Outcome evidence is sectoral and mixed, and external reopening effects remain hard to separate from ruler skill.
